weather_line: Clear above the ridge · eleven hats holding · southwest wind, light

stories.headline: Ministry Confirms Existence of Briefcase; Declines to Confirm Contents; Contents Confirmed to Be Glowing
body: A briefcase of indeterminate origin and pronounced luminescence was logged into the Ministry of Magic's Lost Property repository at 8:47 on Thursday morning, following its discovery on a bench in the Floo Network departure hall by a junior records clerk who described it as 'warm to the touch and humming something I half recognised.'

The Ministry's Department of Mysteries has neither claimed nor denied ownership of the briefcase. A spokesperson issued a statement consisting entirely of the phrase 'This matter is being considered at the appropriate level,' which the assembled press corps noted was seventeen words and contained no information of any kind.
The briefcase remains in Lost Property. It continues to glow. The clerk has been reassigned. Nobody has asked why.

stories.headline: Thursday Opens Quietly at Gringotts; Christine Regards the Quiet with Professional Calm; the Quiet Lasts Until Half Nine
body: Thursday morning at Gringotts was, by any measure, orderly. The main hall was staffed, the ledgers were aligned, and three separate account-holders arrived with correctly completed withdrawal slips — an occurrence which one senior goblin teller, reached for comment, called 'statistically anomalous.'

The quiet ended at 9:31, when a dispute arrived at Christine's desk involving a joint vault, a contested interest calculation dating to the third quarter of last year, and one party who had brought a handwritten note on floral stationery as supporting evidence. Christine read the note, confirmed the arithmetic was wrong on both sides, produced the correct figure from memory, and had the matter filed before the floral stationery was back in the bag.
Both parties left satisfied. The lobby returned to order. A goblin in the third row was seen making a small mark in a notebook, which he declined to explain.

stories.headline: Steve Surveys the Back Step; the Back Step Has Been Fine This Whole Time; Steve Notes It for the Record Anyway
body: Following the successful resolution of the side gate (Tuesday) and the garden latch (Wednesday), Steve conducted a full perimeter survey of the household's remaining exterior fixtures on Thursday afternoon. The back step was found to be level, sound, and in possession of no outstanding concerns whatsoever.

Steve measured it twice. The measurements agreed. He made a note in the household record under 'inspected — no action required,' and stood there for a moment in the manner of a man who would quite like there to be something to fix.

The Jeep, parked nearby and still wearing all eleven of Mrs. Holt's hatted ducks, offered no comment. The enchanted vehicle has not been moved since Wednesday and, sources close to the vehicle suggest, is not in any hurry.

stories.headline: The Eastern Ridgeline Files Its Autumn Notification; Fog Observed Moving into the Hollows; the Gorge Begins Its Seasonal Rearrangement
body: Observers stationed at the upper hollow reported Thursday evening that the fog has begun its characteristic late-August descent into the Red River Gorge — earlier than last year, later than the year before, and precisely on time by the gorge's own accounting, which does not correspond to any calendar in current use.

Trail conditions are assessed as follows: the high ridgeline, firm; the creek crossings, speculative; the rock arches, unchanged and unbothered. The usual enchanted mist was noted wrapping the lower switchbacks by mid-afternoon. Experienced trail-readers will recognise this as the gorge politely suggesting that autumn plans should be forming.
No expeditions are on the docket. The Jeep, however, has been observed facing southeast.

familiars_corner: Lucy: spent the morning in the garden, facing slightly away from the eleven ducks on the Jeep, in the manner of someone who is not looking at something and would like that noted.

Ellie: discovered that the water bowl makes a very small splash if you tap it with one paw, and has been conducting this experiment at intervals throughout the day with no diminishing interest and no conclusion in sight.

Jersey: located the warmest patch of afternoon sunlight, which happened to fall on the back step Steve had just finished inspecting; regards this as a joint achievement and is prepared to share the credit.
founding_editor_note: Back step's level because I poured that foundation even — not bragging, just stating a fact the tape measure already knows. — D.

in_brief.sport: Thursday Invitational Ledger Sprint: Christine finishes; the ledger does not.
in_brief.forecast: Clear through Friday, with an increasing likelihood of Jeep movement and fog in the hollows by the weekend; bring a hat, or borrow one of the ducks'.

storyline_updates.title: The Briefcase
storyline_updates.summary: Day 1: A glowing, humming briefcase of unknown origin has been logged in the Ministry of Magic's Lost Property repository after being found on a bench in the Floo departure hall. The Department of Mysteries has neither claimed nor denied it. The discovering clerk has been reassigned. The briefcase is warm, continues to glow, and nobody has asked why. Day 2 should advance the mystery: perhaps someone attempts to open it (and cannot), or a second Ministry department quietly files a competing claim of ownership, or a witness reports having seen the briefcase before — somewhere else, sometime else, in the wrong order.
